This shift calls for executable world modeling, which integrates two core capabilities: world understanding, reasoning about the underlying structural, mechanical, and causal principles of a world, and executable realization, translating that understanding into a code-based system whose behavior emerges from physical interactions. However, existing benchmarks provide only fragmented evaluations centered on physical reasoning, visual fidelity, or behavioral correctness, leaving the integration of these capabilities insufficiently assessed. To bridge this gap, we introduce ExeWorldBench, to our knowledge the first benchmark to comprehensively evaluate world understanding and executable realization through code-based 3D world construction. ExeWorldBench comprises three progressively challenging tasks: Mechanism Executability, which evaluates the realization of individual mechanisms from visual observations; Compositional Executability, which extends to multi-stage systems with spatial, mechanical, and causal dependencies; and Intent-Driven Executable World Synthesis, which requires constructing executable worlds from high-level goals and physical requirements. Extensive experiments on frontier models reveal substantial limitations in executable world modeling, offering insights into the development of more physically grounded and causally coherent world construction systems.

Computer Vision.title: Robust Pixel-wise Digital Image Correlation under Large Motions and Illumination Variations via a Global-to-Local Hybrid Neural Field
Computer Vision.summary: Digital image correlation (DIC) is a widely used non-contact technique for full-field displacement measurement. Data-driven deep-learning DIC offers rapid inference but may generalize poorly to unseen speckle patterns, deformation modes, noise levels, and illumination conditions. Classical optimization-based DIC and recent image-constrained neural formulations avoid labeled displacement data, yet their convergence and accuracy remain vulnerable to initialization, large rigid-body motion, fine non-uniform deformation, and gray-value disturbances. This paper presents a global-to-local hybrid neural DIC framework for robust pixelwise measurement. Stage 1 estimates a dominant in-plane rigid transformation through coarse rotation search, phase correlation, and masked refinement, providing a reliable initialization under large translation and rotation. Stage 2 represents the residual displacement with a hybrid Kolmogorov-Arnold network (KAN) and multilayer perceptron (MLP), and optimizes it using a valid-overlap, illumination-robust structural loss. The local gray-value model explicitly accommodates multiplicative and additive intensity changes. Simulated and real experiments demonstrate accurate and stable displacement recovery under noise, non-uniform deformation, large rotation, illumination variation, and degraded imaging conditions.

Computer Vision.title: Stabilizing Camera-Controlled Novel View Synthesis at Inference Time
Computer Vision.summary: Training-free, camera-controlled novel view synthesis from a single image using pre-trained video diffusion models often becomes unstable under large camera motion and long generation horizons. Existing approaches commonly combine several inference-time components, making it unclear which design choices are most important for stability. This work identifies the amount of camera motion handled by each diffusion pass as the main factor. CamTrol++ splits the camera path into passes that each cover at most a fixed rotation and generates them one after another, so that every pass stays within the range of motion the backbone handles well. A matched study, in which every setting is scored on the same poses of the same $60^\circ$ orbit, shows that geometric error grows steadily with the arc per pass, while a single SVD pass both loses geometry and tends to freeze the camera. Under one shared camera path, CamTrol++ achieves the lowest epipolar error and the best held-out 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction among CamTrol, NVS-Solver and WAVE, and reaches the quality of CamTrol with the same pass structure at least $3.2\times$ faster. On real RealEstate10K motion it matches CamTrol at half the run time (NVS-Solver is more faithful but $8\times$ slower). The same procedure also improves 3D reconstruction with a second video backbone, LTX-Video. Geometry-constrained spatial attention, color anchoring at pass boundaries and a registration-free warping pipeline that makes warping $6.1\times$ faster complete the framework. The method remains effective for 56-frame generation and under controlled depth corruption. These results show that careful control of camera motion at inference time can substantially improve the stability of camera-controlled novel view synthesis.

Computer Vision.title: Efficient Image Denoising on Smartphone GPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
Computer Vision.summary: Image denoising is a fundamental problem in mobile photography. Despite a large number of solutions proposed for this task, the majority of them are trained on synthetically produced noisy images, and are additionally too computationally heavy for processing full-resolution images on mobile devices. This creates a need for efficient deep learning-based models that are not only performant but can also be deployed on constrained mobile hardware. In this Mobile AI challenge, we address this problem and propose the participants to design fast solutions that can denoise Full HD resolution photos while running on popular smartphone GPUs from Qualcomm and Arm. For this, the participants were provided with a large-scale dataset consisting of noisy-clean image pairs captured in the wild. The runtime of all models was evaluated on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 and Dimensity 9500 chipsets with the Adreno and Mali GPUs, respectively. Top solutions proposed in this challenge are able to perform high-quality image denoising under 100 milliseconds on both platforms while reaching a PSNR score of over 37 dB. A comprehensive description of the models developed in the challenge is provided in this paper.

Computer Vision.title: 4K Image Super-Resolution on Mobile NPUs: Mobile AI 2026 Challenge Report
Computer Vision.summary: Image super-resolution is widely used on mobile devices for upscaling various types of image data. This creates a need for efficient deep learning-based models that are not only performant but can also be deployed on neural processing units (NPUs) present in the majority of mobile and IoT chipsets. In this Mobile AI challenge, we address this problem and propose the participants to design fast solutions that can upsample images from Full HD to 4K resolution while running on popular mobile NPUs from Qualcomm and MediaTek. For this, the participants were provided with the DIV2K dataset and trained models to do an efficient 3X image upscaling. The competition had two tracks: in the first track, the models had to be fully quantized (INT8), and the runtime of all models was evaluated on the Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 NPU. In the second track, the participants were developing floating-point solutions that were evaluated on the MediaTek Dimensity 9500 NPU. Top solutions proposed in this challenge are able to reconstruct 4K images under 5 milliseconds while reaching a PSNR score of 30 dB. A comprehensive description of the models developed in the challenge is provided in this paper.

Computer Vision.title: Vote-in-Context: Turning VLMs into Zero-Shot Rank Fusers
Computer Vision.summary: In the retrieval domain, candidates' fusion from heterogeneous retrievers is a long-standing challenge, particularly for complex, multi-modal data such as videos. While typical fusion techniques are training-free, they rely solely on rank or score signals, disregarding candidates' representations. This work introduces Vote-in-Context (ViC), a generalized, training-free framework that re-thinks list-wise reranking and fusion as a zero-shot reasoning task for a Vision-Language Model (VLM). The core insight is to serialize both content evidence and retriever metadata directly within the VLM's prompt, allowing the model to adaptively weigh retriever consensus against visual-linguistic content. We demonstrate the generality of this framework by applying it to the challenging domain of cross-modal video retrieval. To this end, we introduce the S-Grid, a compact serialization map that represents each video as an image grid, optionally paired with subtitles to enable list-wise reasoning over video candidates. ViC is evaluated both as a single-list reranker, where it dramatically improves the precision of individual retrievers, and as an ensemble fuser, where it consistently outperforms strong baselines like CombSUM. Across video retrieval benchmarks including ActivityNet and VATEX, the framework establishes new state-of-the-art zero-shot retrieval performance, demonstrating its effectiveness in handling complex visual and temporal signals alongside text. In zero-shot settings, ViC achieves Recall@1 scores of 87.1% (t2v) / 89.0% (v2t) on MSR-VTT and 99.6% (v2t) on VATEX, representing massive gains of up to +40 Recall@1 over previous state-of-the-art baselines. We present ViC as a simple, reproducible, and highly effective recipe for turning modern VLMs into powerful zero-shot rerankers and fusers. Code and resources are publicly available at: https://github.com/mohammad2012191/ViC

Computer Vision.title: PSF-Informed Reconstruction: An Enhanced 2D Directional Filtered Backprojection Method for Cone-Beam Rotary Computed Laminography
Computer Vision.summary: Cone-beam rotary computed laminography (CL) presents a viable alternative to cone-beam CT for imaging objects with high aspect ratios. Conventional reconstruction techniques, such as CL-FBP and CL-FDK, often yield suboptimal results charac?terized by pronounced superimposition artifacts, reduced contrast,and blurred edges, primarily due to their reliance on 1D row-wise filtering along detector rows. To address these limitations and improve reconstruction quality, we proposed a novel 2D directional filtered backprojection (DFBP) method based on the point spread function (PSF). First, an exact expression for the projection process is derived by establishing the relationship between a reconstructed pixel and its corresponding projection point on the detector. Second, a revised backprojection process incorporating two weighting factors is introduced to counteract the nonlinearity inherent in conventional backprojection, leading to a simplified PSF formulation. Third, to circumvent the computational burden of 3D image space filtering,an approximate method by linearizing the coordinate relationship in Fourier space under some assumptions is developed that transfers the 3D filtering operation to the 2D projection space. This approach facilitates the derivation of a formally simple yet effective 2D direc?tional filter, which integrates a 2D von Hann window and a 2D sinc window. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method produces reconstructions with superior contrast, sharper boundaries,and fewer superimposition artifacts compared to CL-FBP and CL?FDK. Moreover, it enables more accurate recovery of internal structures, such as bubble defects and electronic components.

Computer Vision.title: What Helps Denoising Can Hurt Memory: Rethinking History in Long Video Generation
Computer Vision.summary: Autoregressive video generators produce long videos block by block, using historical context to maintain temporal consistency. After denoising, a committing pass encodes each clean block into keys and values (KV) that later blocks read, and the same clean block can be encoded into different KV depending on the history it reads. We therefore study historical context not only as a condition for denoising but also as an input to committing. Older historical context that supports denoising can harm subsequent generation when read during committing. At fixed context size and temporal positions, older historical context lowers mean clip-to-clip Subject Consistency. Across 5 generator configurations supporting longer contexts, consistency rises, plateaus, and then declines as committing context expands. Motivated by these findings, we propose Commit Forcing, a training-free rule that organizes committing into a chain. During committing, each block reads only the preceding block's stored KV, so older historical context reaches new entries only through the chain. We apply this rule to 6 pretrained generators. On 60-second VBench, Commit Forcing improves Quality and Total on all 6 generators, by up to 1.27 Quality points and 1.10 Total points. Long-range consistency gains extend to 240-second videos. In a blinded comparison on 120-second LongLive videos, Commit Forcing achieves win rates of 83.5% for subject and scene consistency and 82.9% for overall preference against the base generator, excluding ties.

Computer Vision.title: UI-UG 2: Advancing Mobile UI Understanding and Generation with Fine-Grained Supervision and Reinforcement Learning
Computer Vision.summary: Mobile UI understanding and generation require both fine-grained component perception and reliable structured synthesis. Inspired by the unified direction introduced by UI-UG, we present UI-UG 2, a compact 4B-parameter multimodal large language model (MLLM) that advances mobile UI Understanding and Generation with broader task coverage, a front-end-aligned taxonomy, and online render-aware reinforcement learning. UI-UG 2 constructs a multi-source understanding corpus from RICO, VINS, Android in the Wild, and Android Control, annotated with an 80-category two-level UI taxonomy aligned with front-end component semantics, and pairs it with over 5,000 requirement-screenshot-JSON tuples for progressive structured UI generation through a domain-specific language (DSL). For understanding, UI-UG 2 introduces decomposed rewards for category prediction, OCR fidelity, color recognition, dense grounding, and GUI grounding. Unlike the offline Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)-style generation optimization in UI-UG, UI-UG 2 optimizes generation through end-to-end online Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO): sampled DSL outputs are rendered with a Playwright-based server-side pipeline and evaluated using LLM-as-a-Judge and contrastive preference ranking. Experiments show that UI-UG 2 achieves the strongest referring and dense-grounding results among the evaluated models on our 80-category benchmark, and achieves the best composite generation score among compared models at a compact scale (4B). More importantly, we observe a consistent understanding-to-generation transfer: adding fine-grained UI perception supervision improves generation quality under a fixed training budget, suggesting that component-level semantics provide a shared representational foundation for both tasks.
Computer Vision.comment: 30 pages, 17 figures, 10 tables, including references and appendices

Computer Vision.title: ZOPGA-KD: Zeroth Order PGA Guided Data Free Knowledge Distillation
Computer Vision.summary: Knowledge distillation (KD) enables the transfer of learned representations from a large teacher network to a small student network. In foundational KD, the student network uses the original training data of the teacher model to accomplish this task. However, due to privacy concerns, the original training data is often not available. To overcome this reliance on original training data, several data-free knowledge distillation methods have been developed. Some of these methods operate in the white-box setting, and a few methods generate synthetic data by training a generator network. White-box methods use the teacher model's parameters to obtain a synthetic dataset. To avoid relying on teacher parameters, some methods use computationally expensive generative approaches to obtain such a dataset. There also exist certain black-box methods that generate the synthetic data without accessing teacher parameters. These methods are also computationally intensive. We propose a data-free knowledge distillation method that utilizes just the teacher's output logits and does not require access to its architecture, parameters, or gradients. We generate synthetic data via Projected Gradient Ascent (PGA) starting from smooth random noise signals. Required gradients are obtained through zeroth-order gradient estimation rather than backpropagating through the teacher's parameters. The student is then trained on these synthetically generated samples. We evaluate the proposed method on several benchmark datasets and show that the distillation performance is comparable with approaches that have access to the teacher model parameters.

Computer Vision.title: FilmTogether: Cinematic Video Generation from Low-Cost Inputs
Computer Vision.summary: The widespread adoption of mobile devices has democratized video recording, but a stark aesthetic divide persists between casual, low-cost captures and high-cost cinematic productions. Bridging this gap requires upgrading heterogeneous production elements, such as lighting, specialized costumes, and materials, without altering the core layout, identity, and temporal motion of the original footage. However, this task is heavily bottlenecked by two important challenges: 1) Lacking a high-quality paired training data specifically designed to handle complex low-to-high appearance shifts. 2) Ignoring the capacity of current video editing models to perceive and enhance the multiple low-cost compositions. To address these issues, we present CineCraft-120K, a large-scale dataset of aligned low- and high-cost video pairs annotated with pair-aware editing prompts. CineCraft-120K features a diverse, high-resolution and high-cost Cinematic Crafting bank spanning decades of media production, meticulously taxonomized into 5 broad domains and 23 fine-grained sub-categories. It also provides element-level mapping between low- and high-cost counterparts, offering pair-aware rich textual prompts that precisely detail the required aesthetic transformations while anchoring structural layout. Architecturally, we propose a simple yet effective dual-memory feature adapter, where a text-memory expands semantic capacity for low2high appearance changes, and a hint memory supplies layer-wise visual feature corrections of high-cost element before context injection. Extensive experiments and ablation studies demonstrate the superiority of CineCraft-120K for low-to-high-cost video editing, alongside the effectiveness of our dual-memory adapter.

Computer Vision.title: Selective Linkage Precision for Released Medical Vision-Language Models
Computer Vision.summary: Hospitals may release de-identified chest radiographs while restricting access to their reports. An attacker who already has reports from the same population and their metadata can use a vision-language model (VLM) to match images to reports. We introduce selective linkage precision, which measures correct matches among the highest-confidence queries after filtering candidates by the available attributes. Across 8 public VLMs and 3 chest radiograph datasets, the maximum whole-pool Recall@1 is 0.40%. However, this metric averages over every query without attribute filtering. On ReXGradient-160K, MedSigLIP-448 reaches 67.68% precision at a budget of 100 after filtering by sex, age band, and projection, with a median of 327 candidate reports. On the same eligible query set, an attribute-only policy reaches 24.99% and the model alone reaches 1.98%. Adding acquisition year, available in only 1 of the 3 datasets, yields 99.05% precision and a median of 24 candidates. Uniform guessing on the observed selected queries has an expected precision of 19.91%. Expanding the primary-setting collection to all 123,100 ReXGradient studies lowers precision to 37.23%. On BioViL-T, the tested head finetuning procedures do not lower linkage below the public checkpoint. Selective linkage precision requires inference without retraining and could help hospitals evaluate which attributes to publish.
Computer Vision.comment: Accepted at ML4H 2026 Proceedings, Sydney, Australia

Computer Vision.title: Geometry, Not Statistics: SaluNet for Normalization-Free CNNs and Transformers
Computer Vision.summary: Normalization stabilizes deep networks by adapting intermediate representations through prescribed centering and scaling rules. We investigate the complementary principle: leave representations in their original coordinates and adapt the geometry of the pointwise operator instead. Motivated by controlled evidence that Batch Normalization changes the learning dynamics of parametric activations, we introduce the Saturated Adaptive Linear Unit (SALU), a smooth bounded operator with two learned scalars per layer. A bijective reparameterization exposes its saturation amplitude $S$, transition width $W$, and central gain $S/W$. These coordinates control the bounded forward amplitude and distribute backward sensitivity over the input domain. In a homogeneous mean-field model, forward variance and backward gradient propagation share the normalized coordinate $v/W^2$, where $v$ denotes the activation variance, while obeying distinct stability conditions. We reuse the same primitive to construct the SWALU and GALU adaptive gates and define SaluNet by replacing BN or LN with SALU and conventional activations with SALU-based gates. On CIFAR-100, controlled ResNet-18 experiments show that the complete SALU+SWALU construction outperforms its isolated substitutions. Additional experiments demonstrate trainability down to batch size one, while checkpoint-level representation analysis reveals a broader late-stage spectrum than in the matched BN+ReLU model. ImageNet-1K experiments further demonstrate scalability to ResNet-50 and ViT-B/16, including ViT-B/16 training with an effective batch size of 128. Together, these results support learnable pointwise geometry as a common statistics-free mechanism for signal stabilization and adaptive gating across convolutional networks and vision Transformers.
Computer Vision.comment: Revised version with clarified theoretical analysis, updated experimental results and protocols, and public code and pretrained checkpoints: https://github.com/MouradZaied/SaluNet/

Computer Vision.title: Wave Forcing: Towards Speed-of-Light Streaming Video Generation
Computer Vision.summary: Real-time long-video generation requires continuous output with consistent appearance and natural motion. Existing chunk-wise autoregressive methods face challenges in both generation efficiency and long-video quality: serialized denoising and history-cache refresh require two forward passes even with one-step denoising, and longer rollouts can degrade quality and cause camera drift. We propose Wave Forcing (WF), which co-designs generation, training, and execution for continuous video output with multi-step denoising. WF uses chunk-wise causal attention to access earlier, cleaner chunks before their denoising is complete, and distributes staggered denoising and cache-refresh stages across full-model replicas to achieve 1F1C: one output chunk per concurrent forward round after pipeline fill. To adapt the model to this continuous generation process, we develop a three-stage training procedure that successively introduces mixed-noise denoising, motion supervision, and causal adaptation using self-generated history. To execute this process efficiently, Wave Runtime (WaveRT) uses Wave Parallelism (WP) for early K/V delivery and communication-computation overlap, together with optimized kernels and pipelined VAE decoding. Experiments on Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B show that 5-step WF maintains overall quality comparable to Rolling Forcing while achieving higher Dynamic Degree on both short and long videos. Our system efficiency experiments show that 4-step WF achieves 147.6 DiT FPS and 134.8 end-to-end FPS on eight H200 GPUs, yielding 7.07x the single-GPU end-to-end throughput. In DiT-only tests with matched SageAttention+W8A8 backends, denoising steps, and GPU counts, WP delivers up to 2.53x the throughput of the faster of the Ulysses and Ring context-parallel baselines across six model scales (1.3B-14B).

Computer Vision.title: Toward Counterfactual Learning for Selective Re-Examination in Agentic Visual Search
Computer Vision.summary: Visual search over high-resolution images requires a vision-language model (VLM) not only to determine where to inspect, but also whether another observation is warranted before committing to an answer. Existing prompting, demonstrations, and outcome-based reinforcement learning can encourage re-examination, yet do not directly supervise whether it is beneficial at a particular search state. We introduce ReSee, a benchmark of re-examination decisions comprising 3,227 visual-search trajectories and 8,827 explicit commit-or-re-examine decisions, with counterfactual adjudication that distinguishes states where additional inspection is warranted from those where commitment is preferable. Building on this formulation, we propose CARE (Counterfactual Advantage for Re-Examination), a decision-level reinforcement learning method that compares paired continuations under commit and re-examine verdicts from the same search state. Their cost-aware return difference estimates the counterfactual value of an additional observation and is assigned only to the corresponding verdict tokens, providing localized credit for whether search should continue. Experiments expose limited re-examination selectivity in existing VLMs and show that CARE significantly improves accuracy and decision selectivity over GRPO across two backbones, with higher accuracy and fewer visual requests on six unseen OOD benchmarks.

Computer Vision.title: From Label Priors to Task Evidence: Efficient Long-Video Frame Selection via Bayesian GRPO
Computer Vision.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) face significant scalability challenges in long-video understanding due to quadratic attention complexity and context window constraints. Existing retrieval-based approaches typically rely on supervised learning from static keyframe annotations. However, these label priors often fail to align with the actual information required by downstream MLLMs for complex reasoning, creating a misalignment between the training target and inference needs. To bridge this gap, we propose a probabilistic framework that reformulates frame selection as latent-variable inference. We first initialize a lightweight policy using supervised learning to capture general visual saliency. Then, we treat a frozen MLLM as a task environment and use its answer likelihood as dense task evidence to refine the policy via Bayesian Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO). Within this formulation, the negative log-likelihood (NLL) over ground-truth answer tokens provides a principled dense reward, while a prior-matching KL term preserves semantic consistency with the elicited label prior. This process transitions the selection principle from static label priors to task evidence. Extensive experiments on Video-MME, MLVU, and LongVideoBench demonstrate that our selector achieves competitive accuracy with MLLM-based scorers while retaining the inference efficiency of lightweight methods. The selector is trained once with a frozen MLLM environment and transfers directly to multiple downstream MLLMs without retraining. Code is available at github.com/Miraclecsc/Frame_Selection_GRPO

Computer Vision.title: Beyond Temporal Overlap: Consumer-Aware Evaluation of Sign-Language Segmentation across Three Corpora
Computer Vision.summary: Sign-language segmentation divides continuous signing into clips. In this study, the downstream consumer is a frozen recognizer that assigns one sign label to each predicted clip. Existing metrics instead compare predicted clips with manually annotated boundaries. They do not directly measure whether a clip preserves the visual evidence needed by the recognizer or whether the segmenter produces too many clips. We therefore ask whether overlap metrics and this consumer prefer the same segmenter. We evaluate 27 outputs from three segmentation architectures, three random seeds, and three corpora. Controlled boundary edits separate the effect of removing sign evidence from that of adding surrounding context. Overlap predicts recognition on average, but it does not always determine model choice. At the same intersection-over-union, different recognizers can prefer the shorter or the longer clip. The real outputs reveal two operating regimes. On DGS, overlap, recognition, and sequence error select the same model. On BSL, recognition-based selection recovers and recognizes more reference signs but increases word error rate (WER). Dicta-Sign shows the reverse trade-off: WER selection reduces in-vocabulary WER by 31.17 points but misses more recognizable signs. Segmenters should therefore be evaluated on four axes: temporal agreement, reference recovery, clip recognition, and sequence error, rather than on overlap alone.
Computer Vision.comment: Submitted to IEEE FG 2027. 9 pages, 4 figures. Supplementary material included

Computer Vision.title: Heeding the Inner Voice: Aligning ControlNet Training via Intermediate Features Feedback
Computer Vision.summary: Despite significant progress in text-to-image diffusion models, achieving precise spatial control over generated outputs remains challenging. One of the popular approaches for this task is ControlNet, which introduces an auxiliary conditioning module into the architecture. To improve alignment of the generation image and control, ControlNet++ proposes a cycle consistency loss to refine correspondence between controls and outputs, but restricts its application to the final denoising steps, while the main structure is introduced at an early stage of generation. To address this issue, we suggest InnerControl -- a training strategy that enforces spatial consistency across a broad range of diffusion steps, including early high-noise ones. Specifically, we train lightweight control prediction probes -- small convolutional networks -- to reconstruct input control signals (e.g., edges, depth) from intermediate diffusion features across denoising steps. We show empirically that such models can extract signals even from very noisy latents and utilize these models to generate pseudo ground truth controls during training. Suggested approach enables alignment loss that minimizes the difference between predicted and target condition over most of the diffusion trajectory. Our experiments demonstrate that our method improves control alignment, with perceptual fidelity preserved or improved in most settings and small FID trade-offs in others. Our approach can be applied to both UNet- and Transformer-based diffusion architectures and be integrated with established training techniques (e.g., ControlNet++) to achieve high performance across different condition methods such as edge, segmentation and depth conditions.
Computer Vision.comment: The project page is available at \url{https://controlgenai.github.io/InnerControl/}

Computer Vision.title: Learning-based Axial Video Motion Magnification
Computer Vision.summary: Video motion magnification amplifies invisible small motions to be perceptible, which provides humans with a spatially dense and holistic understanding of small motions in the scene of interest. This is based on the premise that magnifying small motions enhances the legibility of motions. In the real world, however, vibrating objects often possess convoluted systems that have complex natural frequencies, modes, and directions. Existing motion magnification often fails to improve legibility since the intricate motions still retain complex characteristics even after being magnified, which may distract us from analyzing them. In this work, we focus on improving legibility by proposing a new concept, axial motion magnification, which magnifies decomposed motions along the user-specified direction. Axial motion magnification can be applied to various applications where motions of specific axes are critical, by providing simplified and easily readable motion information. To achieve this, we propose a novel Motion Separation Module that enables to disentangle and magnify the motion representation along axes of interest. Furthermore, we build a new synthetic training dataset for the axial motion magnification task. Our proposed method improves the legibility of resulting motions along certain axes by adding a new feature: user controllability. Axial motion magnification is a more generalized concept; thus, our method can be directly adapted to the generic motion magnification and achieves favorable performance against competing methods.
Computer Vision.comment: Presented at European Conference on Computer Vision (ECCV) 2024. Project page (code&dataset): https://axial-momag.github.io/axial-momag/

Computer Vision.title: ODC: Orthogonal Drift Correction for Improved Text-to-Image Semantic Alignment at Inference
Computer Vision.summary: Text-to-image models have achieved remarkable success in generating high-quality images from textual descriptions. However, they often struggle with "semantic drift," where the generated output fails to precisely align with complex or nuanced text prompts. While recent approaches have attempted to address semantic errors regarding attribute binding or object presence, there remains a gap for a more holistic method that addresses these issues by directly refining the text embeddings of the initial user prompt. In this work, we introduce Orthogonal Drift Correction (ODC), an inference-time guidance method designed to mitigate semantic drift without requiring model retraining or additional user inputs. ODC guides image generation through a two-stage process. In the first stage, it identifies the semantic drift by evaluating the initially generated image against the user prompt in a shared vision-language embedding space. It then isolates the component of this drift vector that is orthogonal to the prompt's direction and translates it back into text via a vocabulary-based surrogate mechanism. In the second stage, it produces refined text conditioning for a second generation pass by feeding both the initial text embedding and the re-embedded drift representation into an adaptive rank-reduced concept removal module. Our experiments demonstrate that ODC consistently improves prompt-image alignment, increasing CLIP scores by up to 5.4% over the baseline on the COALBench-300 and PartiPrompts benchmarks. Furthermore, on the T2I-CompBench complex subset, ODC improves the average 3-in-1 score by 4.5% over the competing methods. As a plug-and-play module, ODC offers a practical and efficient method for improving the reliability of text-to-image models. Code is available at https://github.com/kasrakamali/ODC.
Computer Vision.comment: Accepted to Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR) 2026

Computer Vision.title: SHIFT: Steering Hidden Intermediates in Flow Transformers
Computer Vision.summary: Diffusion models have become the leading approach for high-fidelity image generation, with recent DiT-based models achieving strong prompt adherence and high visual quality. However, removing unwanted concepts from these models typically requires expensive gradient-based fine-tuning, which is particularly prohibitive for multi-billion-parameter Diffusion Transformers and incompatible with distilled variants. We propose SHIFT, a simple model-weight-update-free inference-time framework for concept suppression in DiT models via targeted manipulation of intermediate activations at inference time, inspired by activation steering in LLMs. SHIFT learns steering vectors from contrastive prompts and applies them dynamically. We demonstrate that a single time-independent steering vector generalizes across all denoising timesteps and that vectors computed on a distilled model transfer effectively to its non-distilled counterpart without recomputation. SHIFT achieves strong concept suppression while preserving prompt fidelity and image quality. The same mechanism also enables flexible control -- adding, removing, or changing objects and styles without retraining. SHIFT targets hosted inference settings: it does not remove the concept from the model weights and is therefore complementary to weight-level unlearning.
Computer Vision.comment: The project page is available at \url{https://controlgenai.github.io/SHIFT}

Computer Vision.title: UniCaMo: Unified Camera and Motion Control for Video Diffusion Models
Computer Vision.summary: We present \textbf{UniCaMo}, an unified framework for joint control of camera and object motion in image-and-text-to-video diffusion models. Given a reference image, text prompt, sparse 3D object trajectories, and a 3D camera trajectory, UniCaMo constructs motion-consistent input noise that directly encodes the desired motion. Our 3D-grounded noise construction combines reference-derived noise propagation with a spherical Gaussian noise representation for newly revealed regions, providing a simple and effective motion prior without requiring reconstruction of unseen scene geometry. UniCaMo requires no architectural modifications or dedicated control modules and can be adapted using lightweight LoRA fine-tuning with low training data volume. Experiments on standard controllable video generation benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art motion controllability and high visual quality with minimal inference overhead.
Computer Vision.comment: Qualitative videos are available on our project page: https://phongnhhn.info/Unicamo/

Computer Vision.title: Training-free Conditional Object Composition for Multi-object Image Generation with Diffusion Models
Computer Vision.summary: Multi-object image generation in text-to-image diffusion models remains challenging, as existing approaches struggle to reliably generate all objects specified in a prompt. Compositional approaches that generate objects independently often fail to capture the interactions among them, whereas joint generation methods tend to suffer from inter-object interference. In this work, we propose a training-free framework, termed conditional object composition, that relaxes joint generation methods by taking one step back toward compositional approaches. Our framework decomposes the generation of $N$ objects into two stages: it first generates a subset of $N-1$ objects and then composes the remaining object conditioned on the generated content. To enable effective composition, we adopt an inpainting-based formulation with layout guidance to preserve existing regions and encourage spatially coherent placement. To address the challenge of selecting which objects to generate separately, we introduce an attention-based scoring mechanism based on cross-attention maps and further explore the use of off-the-shelf object detectors. We evaluate our method on multi-object image generation using the widely adopted MS COCO dataset. Experimental results show that our approach achieves competitive or improved performance compared to existing methods, particularly as the number of objects increases. Further studies highlight the importance of the proposed design choices. The source code is available at https://github.com/ShampooWang/condComp_imageGen/tree/main
Computer Vision.comment: Accepted for oral presentation at TAAI 2026

Computer Vision.title: Dual-Grained Policy Optimization for Hallucination Reduction in Flow-Based RL
Computer Vision.summary: Reinforcement Fine-Tuning (RFT) on flow-based models is crucial for alignment. However, they often introduce visual hallucinations like over-optimized details and semantic misalignment. This work explains why visual hallucinations arise and shows how to reduce them. We first investigate RFT methods from a unified perspective and trace hallucinations to two mechanisms. Limited exploration from stochastic differential equation (SDE) rollouts yields detail-dominated within-group differences, leading to fine-grained optimization that over-emphasizes local details and neglects global semantics. Trajectory imitation writes reward-selected SDE noise into the velocity field, leading to inconsistent optimization that degrades cross-step consistency. Building on this, we propose DGPO, a general framework to mitigate hallucinations. Specifically, we design Dynamic Granularity Rollout (DGR) to balance global semantics and local details by dynamically scheduling noise sources. We then introduce a Consistent Policy Gradient Optimization that preserves the consistency by aligning the policy with a more stable prior. Experiments show that DGPO reduces low-/high-level hallucinations by 49%/38% and improves the average of out-of-domain (OoD) metrics by +4.9% on FLUX.1.dev, compared with the baseline's -0.7%. Project page: https://xiaofeng-tan.github.io/projects/ConsistentRFT/

Computer Vision.title: Crop Mapping Evaluation under Sampling Bias
Computer Vision.summary: Government agencies use crop maps to estimate production, monitor food security, and set agricultural policy. These crop maps are usually validated against field labels, but these labels are rarely a random sample of the area the map covers. Field teams tend to label parcels near roads and skip ones that are small or hard to reach, so performance measured on held-out labels mainly describes the places they visited. We call the difference between this reported performance and performance over the whole mapped region the deployment performance gap. To estimate performance over the whole region, we use a weighted form of prediction-powered inference (PPI). The classifier's predictions on unlabeled points across the region give a first estimate, and its errors on the labeled points correct that estimate, with more weight on labels from under-sampled conditions. We test this in five European regions where crop registers label every declared parcel, so the true performance is known. Simulating six documented collection practices there produces gaps of up to 0.20 macro-F1. On the collection rule that creates the largest gap in each region, 5 km block cross-validation still overestimates macro-F1 by as much as 0.18, while PPI with weights estimated from satellite embeddings reduces the largest error across regions to 0.07. Importance-weighted cross-validation with the same weights does almost as well, so most of the improvement comes from the weights themselves. We also apply the method to three Kenyan datasets that have no region-wide reference labels. For a roadside dataset collected with helmet-mounted cameras, the estimated macro-F1 falls from 0.93 under random cross-validation to 0.61, although the correction relies on a small number of heavily weighted labels. Our code is available at https://github.com/microsoft/pappi.

Computer Vision.title: PhoneValue-Bench: A Multimodal Benchmark and Datasets for Consumer Smartphone Recommerce Valuation
Computer Vision.summary: As consumer smartphone recommerce scales, buyers must quote binding repurchase prices from seller-uploaded multi-view photos and diagnostic screenshots before devices reach the warehouse. Accurate remote valuation requires fusing noisy cosmetic evidence with identity, battery, lock, and channel risk from screenshots and staff forms, since an error in any modality changes both grade and payout. However, existing multimodal resources mainly target general VLM competence, screen reading, or factory defect detection, and largely overlook staff-aligned trade-in fields, dual appearance/staff ground truth, and executable valuation scorecards. This gap stems from two challenges: (1) the lack of large-scale real trade-in data with audited dual annotations and a compact ranking benchmark kept separate from training labels, and (2) the need to jointly reason over unordered multi-view cosmetics and diagnostic screens under operational deduction rules. To address these challenges, we propose PhoneValue-Bench, a dual-GT evaluation suite with tier-gated scorecards, together with PhoneValue-Corpus, a matched weakly labeled training set of over twenty thousand orders and hundreds of thousands of captioned images. We further present ValueAgent, a staged perception-fusion-valuation reference pipeline aligned with production inspection, plus an executable public scorer and submission schema. Experiments show that ValueAgent reaches a measured 84.1/100 on Bench-Full, with 97.0 appearance fill and 54.1 staff-field fill, establishing a practical dual-GT benchmark for multimodal recommerce valuation.

Computer Vision.title: Parsed Text Understates Vision-Language Models: From Below to Above Expert Agreement on Fine-Grained Facial Emotion
Computer Vision.summary: EmoNet-Face-HQ is a benchmark of 2,500 generated portraits, each rated by four psychology experts on 40 emotion categories. It concludes that vision-language models (VLMs) on average offer no dependable improvement over random guessing and that a fine-tuned model is required. The benchmark reads each model's answer from generated text, and its zero-shot prompt demands a fixed number of emotions per face. Its own results already show that this protocol can decide the outcome: one VLM moves from chance to close to expert agreement when only the prompt changes. We keep the images, expert ratings and metric and change only how the answer is asked for and read: one yes/no question per category, scored by the probability of "yes". Scored from parsed text on the five categories experts agree on most, eleven open-weight VLMs average a quadratic-weighted $κ$ of 0.425 against individual experts, below the 0.468 at which two experts agree. Scored from yes-probabilities, the same models average 0.553, and all eleven agree with an individual expert better than a second expert does. The VLMs' mean is level with the benchmark's fine-tuned model (0.555), and three of them significantly exceed it without any training. Only one exceeds a stricter reference, the mean of three experts scored against the fourth (0.563). Verdicts that VLMs fail at graded facial affect ratings may therefore describe the readout more than the model. A fine-tuned model should have to beat a pretrained VLM read this way before it is called necessary, and the benchmark's own does not clearly do so.
Computer Vision.comment: Preprint. 10 pages, 2 figures; 10-page supplementary material as ancillary file. This work has been submitted to the IEEE for possible publication. Copyright may be transferred without notice, after which this version may no longer be accessible

Computer Vision.title: CheXPoT: Post-Hoc Visual Verification and Correction of VLM-Generated Radiology Reports
Computer Vision.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) have shown promise for chest radiograph report generation, but adoption remains limited because of hallucinated findings that are not grounded in the image. Correcting these hallucinations and improving overall report quality remains a significant challenge. Prior work has addressed this problem by refining models with reinforcement learning, preference optimization, or chain-of-thought supervision, often at substantial compute cost. To address this gap, we introduce CheXPoT, a program-of-thought (PoT) framework that verifies each generated finding against image features and removes those it cannot ground. CheXPoT decomposes generated reports into predicates with RadGraph and an LLM, grounds these predicates against a DenseNet-121 and Grad-CAM visual evidence table, executes PoT verification code, and rewrites reports after removing unsupported predicates. On a 4,145-image held-out split, CheXPoT yields statistically significant precision gains on 8 of 14 CheXpert classes and F1 gains on 5, with no significant decreases in either metric. CheXPoT lifts micro-average precision from 19.2% (MedGemma-4B) to 46.8% (MedGemma-4B + CheXPoT) and micro-average F1 from 23.0% to 49.4%, absolute gains of 27.6% and 26.4% respectively. We also tested CheXPoT on other VLM report generators. On LLaVA-Med, CheXPoT lifts micro-average precision from 4.5% to 17.7% and micro-average F1 from 6.3% to 19.4%. On MAIRA-2, CheXPoT lifts micro-average precision from 15.6% to 42.1% and micro-average F1 from 21.0% to 45.3%. Our results suggest that inexpensive post-hoc visual verification may improve VLM trustworthiness by correcting unsupported findings from generated reports. CheXPoT lays a foundation for tools that help validate VLM-generated radiology reports and reduce unsupported findings. These innovations may subsequently help increase trust and adoption of VLM tools in Medicine.

Computer Vision.title: ConstraintMatch: Compositional Image-Text Matching through Constrained Regional Evidence Selection
Computer Vision.summary: Local image--text matching can find strong evidence for individual concepts yet favor captions with incorrect attribute--entity bindings. We introduce ConstraintMatch, a training-free inference method that turns entity-level regional consistency into an explicit matching cost. On the same frozen condition--region similarity matrix, it compares independent crop selection for each category and attribute with a shared crop choice within each entity. Their gap quantifies the score advantage obtained by relaxing the shared-region constraint. Spatial references from the same image calibrate this gap by keeping category evidence fixed while jointly shifting an entity's attribute maps. Per-entity clipping prevents cancellation across residuals, and the scaled mean cost is subtracted from global similarity. ConstraintMatch uses pooled embeddings, and spatial calibration requires no additional encoder calls. With parameters fixed per backbone across tasks, ConstraintMatch improves over global matching by 7.70 percentage points on full ARO Attribute and 5.63 points on held-out SugarCrepe++ attribute swaps, averaged across Qwen~2B and CORE~2B. Against SGI adapted to the same 13-crop budget, the respective gains are 4.85 and 3.51 points. Controlled analyses distinguish the effects of shared-region matching and candidate score calibration. The results establish entity-level evidence selection as a practical scoring principle for compositional multimodal retrieval.

Computer Vision.title: Transfer the Style, Not the Semantics: Mitigating Semantic Leakage in Image-Guided Stylization
Computer Vision.summary: Image-guided zero-shot style transfer enables training-free stylization of arbitrary content images using a reference style. Despite recent progress, existing methods commonly rely on self-attention manipulation to inject style information, which may transfer semantic content from the style image, leading to semantic leakage. In this work, we revisit this phenomenon from the perspective of key--value coupling in the self-attention of diffusion models. Our analysis shows that the native correspondence between style keys and values plays an important role in transferring semantic information from the style image. Motivated by this observation, we propose SuRe, a timestep-aware key--value regulation framework that mitigates semantic leakage by disrupting the native key--value correspondence while progressively restoring it for faithful style transfer. Specifically, we present value shuffle to decouple style keys and values while preserving the empirical distribution of the values, together with a progressive recoupling mechanism that gradually recouples them throughout the stylization process. Experiments against 18 representative methods demonstrate that SuRe maintains competitive style similarity while consistently improving content similarity across SD1.5, SDXL, SD3, and FLUX.1-dev, with natural generalization to multi-style transfer. The code will be publicly available at https://github.com/XinR-Tang/SuRe.

Computer Vision.title: Now You See Them, Now You Dont FusionGhost Gait for Occlusion-Robust Gait Recognition with ArabGait dataset
Computer Vision.summary: Skeleton-based gait recognition is generally more robust to appearance changes than pixel-based methods, but this robustness depends on stable pose extraction. Clothing variation in gait recognition includes changes in garments, silhouette, and carried items; under Gulf clothing (Kandoora/Abaya), the dominant failure mode shifts from appearance change to lower-limb pose degradation caused by severe occlusion. To study this regime, we introduce ArabGait, a 45-subject indoor multi-view dataset with four walking conditions across three viewpoints, and show that Gulf clothing lowers mean lower-limb confidence from 0.811 to 0.683 and raises lower-limb failure rate from 7.98% to 17.82%, with ankles most affected. We propose FusionGhost-Gait, a fused spatiotemporal architecture that integrates spatial graph blocks and temporal modeling in one residual unit, removes redundant channel projections, and uses compact temporal Ghost kernels as a lightweight regularization mechanism for pose-noisy trajectories while preserving efficient temporal downsampling. On ArabGait cross-clothing evaluation, including Protocol A and Protocol B, FusionGhost-Gait reaches up to 67.91% Rank-1 while remaining compact (108,970- 133,674 parameters and 0.035-0.052 billion floating-point operations (GFLOPs)), achieving more than 65% fewer parameters and 75% lower FLOPs than existing baselines. These results indicate that the proposed model generalizes effectively to challenging Gulf-clothing conditions while remaining lightweight and deployable for surveillance and access-control biometric systems.
Computer Vision.comment: Submitted to "Engineering Applications of Artificial Intelligence", Elsevier

Computer Vision.title: ProtoSemImage: Image-Valued Prototypes with Deformable Row Alignment for Interpretable Document Classification
Computer Vision.summary: Prototypes in classification models are almost always vectors, and a vector has no readable form. This paper asks what happens when a prototype is an image. Documents give the question a natural form, because a document can be rendered as a multi-channel image in which every token becomes a pixel, so a class representative can take the same shape and the same channel semantics as the inputs it stands for. ProtoSemImage represents each class by one or more visual archetypes: prototype images in a four-channel HSV space whose channels carry named linguistic factors. A Skip-Gram objective learns that color space end to end through a four-dimensional bottleneck, discourse boundary rows become differentiable typed difference rows, and classification reduces to 2D visual template matching: a deformable row alignment between a document image and the archetype bank, in the spirit of dynamic time warping. Because the match is a spatial pattern comparison rather than a linear readout, the model reports where an input departs from its archetype and along which channel, and a generative head decodes each archetype back into text. The image representation works: it beats an otherwise identical model with vector prototypes in all three paired seeds, by between 4.3 and 11.8 points on a ten-class task. The distance-based matching does not. A diagnostic that keeps the representation fixed and swaps only the classifier recovers the sequence baselines, which locates a 20.6-point shortfall in the matching rather than in the color compression, and a benchmark built so that a pair of documents shares a bag of words and differs only in arrangement confirms the layout-preservation it was designed for. We report both directions, because for a representation whose whole purpose is inspect ability, the failure modes are as informative as the gains.

Computer Vision.title: DADKC: Distribution-Aware Adaptive Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation for Cloth-Hybrid Lifelong Person Re-identification
Computer Vision.summary: Lifelong Person Re-identification (LReID) aims to match the same person using sequentially collected data. In practical long-term deployments, however, the model must handle both domain shifts across cameras and scenes, and irregular clothing changes of the same identity. This gives rise to the Cloth-Hybrid Lifelong Person Re-identification (CH-LReID) task, which demands balancing cloth-relevant and cloth-irrelevant knowledge in streaming data. While existing LReID methods have explored replay-based or distillation-based anti-forgetting strategies, they typically fail to sufficiently model stage-aware domain distributions and cross-stage feature continuity under exemplar-free training. To address this problem, we propose a Distribution-Aware Adaptive Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation (DADKC) framework. The core idea is to enhance the existing Differentiated Knowledge Consolidation (DKC) paradigm with adaptive distribution modeling. To this end, three lightweight modules are designed: (1) an Anchor Pool Adapter (APA) to retrieve learnable anchor cues for refining identity features; (2) a Phase Path Mixer (PPM) to perform stage-aware expert routing for integrating domain-specific distribution paths; and (3) a Stage Bridge Alignment (SBA) module to regularize the continuity of base, anchor, and path representations between adjacent stages. Extensive experiments on the CH-LReID and LReID benchmarks show that DADKC gains 4.1%/4.5% mAP/R1 on Order-1 and 3.6%/3.4% mAP/R1 on Order-2 over the DKC baseline, and lowers weighted forgetting from 2.4%/1.7% to 1.8%/1.4%, while storing neither historical images nor per-image features. The code is available at https://github.com/fire667/DADKC.

Computer Vision.title: The MASSIMAL Dataset: UAV Hyperspectral Images and Ground Truth Observations for Coastal Habitat Mapping in Norway
Computer Vision.summary: The MASSIMAL dataset was collected in an effort to develop new remote sensing methods for mapping shallow water coastal habitats, such as kelp forests, seagrass meadows and maerl beds. The main component of the dataset is a set of hyperspectral images collected using a unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). Images were collected during 45 UAV flights performed at 4 main areas along the Norwegian coast, spanning across a wide latitude range, from 59 to 67 degrees north. The ground sampling distance of the hyperspectral images is 3.5 cm, and the spectral range is 400-1000 nm, sampled across 300 spectral bands. During acquisition, push-broom imagery was automatically split into images with a maximum along-track length of 2000 lines. Out of approximately 1000 hyperspectral images, 221 have been annotated, using segmentation masks and a hierarchical taxonomy. An open source image processing pipeline has been developed as part of the dataset preparation, enabling efficient generation of reflectance images and glint-corrected images based on published radiance images. The dataset also includes color images (RGB) and multispectral images collected using UAV, and georeferenced image mosaics constructed from these. Ground truth data supporting the remote sensing images include hours of underwater video, thousands of geotagged underwater images, and tens of kilometers of single-beam sonar data. The data provide a foundation for assessing habitat distribution, tracking changes, and evaluating ecosystem services, thus supporting evidence-based management in Norwegian coastal environments.
Computer Vision.comment: 25 pages, 8 figures. Submitted to Scientific Data (part of Nature portfolio)

Computer Vision.title: Old Is Not False: Valid-Time Memory for Interactive Video World Models
Computer Vision.summary: Interactive video world models draw each frame from a memory bank of earlier frames stamped with their capture times. With frames, weights and noise fixed, reversing the timestamps of two views flips the state that generators of two families draw: they take the newest timestamp as the truth. That reading is right as long as states never return. After an agent undoes an action, the newest view of a region is outdated and the only view of the present is older; memories for changing worlds delete that older view, and memories that keep it hand the generator the past. Temporal databases separate when a record is stored from when its content holds, its valid time. ReDate keeps every frame and dates each retrieved token by its valid time, read from the agent's action log. The frozen generator then reads a reverted region as one that has just reached a new state, so ReDate needs no training. We prove that trusting the newest timestamp is right exactly when every current view is dated after every outdated one, that without a view taken after the return only the action log tells a reverted region from an up-to-date one, and that a generator able to draw from its own prediction gains more from re-dating than from deletion when the moved tokens keep little weight. After an undo, ReDate raises the share of FAR's steps showing the current state from 0.36 to 0.62 and HY-WorldPlay's from 0.003 to 0.19. We also propose a calibrated state metric to test any memory after undos.

Computer Vision.title: SceneBound: How Much Should a Streaming 3D Reconstruction Model Remember?
Computer Vision.summary: Streaming 3D reconstruction models keep past video frames in a recurrent state, fast weights from test-time training, or a key-value (KV) cache. Each written frame shifts the coordinate frame of later cameras or occupies GPU memory. Training-free rules decide what to write from a signal of the current frame. How much they write accounts for their mean accuracy: spending the update budget of a gate at uniformly spaced frames, with no signal, matches nine published gates, and the budget bounds the drift of the state wherever the writes fall. We propose SceneBound, a training-free rule that writes a frame only when its predicted camera pose lies at least a fixed radius from every stored keyframe. Its keyframe count stays within a constant factor of the covering number of the visited poses, the fewest views that keep a keyframe near every camera, so the count grows with the places visited and stays flat when the camera returns. In large scenes, SceneBound closes a submap once decoding its first frame again reveals drift. SceneBound uses one radius across four released models and three memory types. In the recurrent state of CUT3R and the KV cache of StreamVGGT, it achieves the lowest mean trajectory error among the published training-free rules we evaluate, in one pass and over nine passes of a scene, where its keyframes grow by 3% to 6%.

Computer Vision.title: Efficient and Robust Video Defense Framework against 3D-field Personalized Talking Face
Computer Vision.summary: Talking Face Generation (TFG) has made remarkable progress in synthesizing realistic speaker videos, evolving into two paradigms based on identity incorporation: image-based 2D TFG and video-based 3D TFG. Despite enabling efficient content creation, TFG also raises risks of unauthorized portrait forgery and privacy abuse, motivating proactive defenses. Existing defenses mainly target image-based 2D TFG, while, to our knowledge, no proactive defense has been developed for video-based 3D TFG. A straightforward solution is to apply existing image-based defenses independently to each video frame. However, experiments show that this adaptation is ineffective and computationally expensive: video-based 3D TFG lacks the image-reference modules and reverse diffusion processes exploited by existing defenses, and per-frame optimization incurs substantial overhead. To address this gap, we analyze the vulnerabilities of video-based 3D TFG and propose ErodedFace, an efficient proactive defense framework targeting reference-video preprocessing. ErodedFace uses a curriculum-inspired two-stage strategy: Stage I establishes scale-robust disruption through similarity-guided parameter inheritance and adaptive multi-scale optimization; Stage II improves perceptual fidelity and transformation robustness without weakening protection. Extensive experiments show that ErodedFace effectively protects portrait videos against unauthorized video-based 3D TFG, achieves a 10.0x speedup in defense generation over existing image-based 2D TFG defenses, and remains robust to common transformations and recent purification methods.

Computer Vision.title: SAVIER: Source-Anchored Visual Inspection and Evidence-Guided Repair for Vietnamese Cultural Text-to-Image Generation
Computer Vision.summary: We present SAVIER, a training-free, one-pass framework that repairs the depiction of a named Vietnamese cultural entity in a generated image while preserving the scene details requested by the user. The problem is hard because a plausible scene can miss the cues that identify the entity, and prompt-level refinement never inspects the image it produces. SAVIER starts from a Culture-TRIP expanded prompt; a Curator separates source-linked cultural cues from prompt-preservation requirements, a prompt-blind Observer describes the first image, and a Refiner turns the discrepancies into at most three positive instructions before one regeneration with the same seed and a fixed bank of reference photographs. On the 50 bilingual prompts of ViCuP, evaluated with SDXL and FLUX.1-dev against a frozen, human-verified visual contract, SAVIER raises contract fulfillment from 55.6 to 69.6 and from 59.1 to 67.3 over Culture-TRIP and raises CAIRE cultural relevance on FLUX.1-dev. A reference-only ablation that removes the agent repair shows that SAVIER's photographs account for most of the contract gain; the agent roles add country-level relevance on FLUX.1-dev without lowering adherence to the original prompt under the official VQAScore. Project page: https://oxyzgiahuy.github.io/savier/

Computer Vision.title: Large Discrete Policy: Advancing Explicit Behavior Modeling with Stochastic Iterative Scoring
Computer Vision.summary: Behavior policies are often formulated as continuous generative models, whose iterative denoising processes are expressive but difficult to interpret and prone to producing implausible actions. We propose the Large Discrete Policy (LDiP), a fully discrete behavior modeling framework that selects actions from a large vocabulary of physically plausible candidates. Rather than perturbing actions, LDiP improves expressivity through stochastic iterative scoring: it progressively re-scores and prunes candidates with score-space stochasticity, enabling fine-grained ranking and exploration among plausible actions while preserving an explicit decision process. Across end-to-end planning, closed-loop driving, robotic manipulation, and vision-language-action settings, LDiP consistently outperforms strong discrete and continuous baselines in autonomous driving, and exceeds or matches continuous generative policies in robotic manipulation. These results show that discrete policies, when equipped with effective scoring mechanisms, offer an expressive, plausible, and interpretable alternative for behavior modeling. Project website: https://zhenxinli.net/LargeDiscretePolicy/.

Computer Vision.title: Adversarial robustness does not entail human-aligned categorization
Computer Vision.summary: Adversarial training can improve some forms of correspondence between artificial and biological vision, but whether robust classifiers acquire human-aligned classification behavior remains unclear. We generated 1,008 controversial stimuli by optimizing latent inputs to a pretrained GAN to elicit high-confidence disagreements between pairs of robust ImageNet classifiers. We compared four adversarially robust ImageNet classifiers - ResNet-101, ViT-B, ConvNeXt-L, and Swin-L - with two-alternative category judgments from 60 participants. We first evaluated each classifier on stimuli optimized to elicit disagreement with another model. Across classifiers, accuracy in predicting individual participants' single-trial category choices was near chance (48.6-51.3%), whereas majority judgments from other participants predicted responses with 85.0-86.8% accuracy. An analysis incorporating model prediction strength and participants' reported confidence found weak positive model-human correspondence for the two convolutional models. On stimuli optimized for disagreement between other model pairs, all four robust classifiers predicted human responses above chance but less accurately than predictions based on other participants' majority judgments; the same pattern held for 17 additional RobustBench models not used in stimulus generation. Across these 17 models, mean model-participant agreement was 67.3%, versus 81.3% mean participant-participant agreement on the same images. These results identify model-specific failures of human alignment and a model-human mismatch that persists across robust classifiers and substantially exceeds disagreement among human observers. Our findings show that adversarial robustness alone does not guarantee human-aligned categorization and suggest that robustness and human alignment should be evaluated as distinct properties of visual recognition systems.

Computer Vision.title: IMPose: Closed-Loop Correction Propagation for Interactive Multi-Person Pose Annotation
Computer Vision.summary: High-quality dynamic human pose annotations provide important supervision for learning fine-grained human motion, yet dense multi-person video annotation remains labor-intensive. Sparse human corrections can reduce this effort, but their propagated locations may become unreliable and ambiguous across identities. Existing interactive refinement and temporal propagation methods do not explicitly address how imperfect propagated corrections should participate in subsequent multi-person pose inference. We propose IMPose, a correction-conditioned temporal inference framework for interactive multi-person pose annotation. IMPose separates temporal correspondence from pose estimation: propagated corrections are treated as geometric priors rather than final predictions and are refined by a correction-aware decoder using target-frame visual evidence. A keypoint-aware identity state further combines structured pose geometry with trajectory history to preserve person- and joint-level correspondence. The refined pose and identity state are fed back to subsequent frames, forming a closed temporal correction loop. Under a controlled sparse-correction protocol on PoseTrack21, one correction improves mean average precision (mAP) from 38.87 to 67.99 and Higher Order Tracking Accuracy (HOTA) from 52.21 to 64.89. At a 20-frame correction interval, IMPose achieves 89.03% keypoint-level Object Keypoint Similarity (K-OKS), compared with 81.41% for CoTracker and 70.12% for PoseWarper-based propagation. We further extend PoseTrack21 with 188K additional person instances through 3.55M annotation updates to keypoints, bounding boxes, and person IDs using 100 annotator-hours. The annotation tool, code, and extended dataset will be released.

Computer Vision.title: Learnable Hodge-Laplacian Driven Mixture of Experts for Steady-PDE Surrogates on Coarse Unstructured Meshes
Computer Vision.summary: Current approaches for steady partial differential equations surrogate models on unstructured meshes apply a single mixing mechanism to the whole solution. This paper proposes an architecture that partitions the solution among vanilla transformer experts, each focused on a different spectral scale. The partition is built from a discrete Hodge Laplacian $L_0=\star_0^{-1} d_0^{\top}\star_1 d_0$, that serves as a fitting layer measuring high-frequency content. A gating mechanism takes the mesh as input and produces the per-vertex weights that recombine the expert outputs. AirFRANS is a steady Reynolds-averaged Navier--Stokes (RANS) airfoil benchmark. We evaluate our approach in a reduced remeshed version of the benchmark with each unstructured mesh counting 9.6K faces and 4.9K vertices. We compare our approach with the Transolver on the same dataset and dataset slit. Our approach reduces relative $L_2$ error by 31% and interior mean squared error by 47%.

Computer Vision.title: LoD-Loc v4: Towards Generalized Aerial Visual Localization via Panoptic LoD 3D Map Registration
Computer Vision.summary: Aerial visual localization over Level-of-Detail (LoD) 3D Maps has recently gained significant traction due to its global scalability, storage efficiency, and privacy-preserving nature. However, existing methods rely almost exclusively on building elements, which leads to catastrophic localization failures in rural or undeveloped areas where buildings are sparse or non-existent. To address this, we construct a unified Panoptic LoD 3D Map by fusing OpenStreetMap (OSM), Digital Elevation Models (DEM), and LoD assets, reformulating the problem as a panoptic registration task. By parsing the query image into discrete building `thing' instances and continuous `stuff' regions comprising road, vegetation, and water, we establish a holistic alignment with this map to robustly optimize the camera pose. To enable reliable panoptic perception, we develop a new automated pipeline that constructs AirPan - the largest aerial panoptic segmentation dataset to date, comprising 85k images with pixel-accurate annotations. This empowers our panoptic segmentation model to exhibit remarkable zero-shot generalization capabilities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that LoD-Loc v4 consistently outperforms state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines by a significant margin. Most notably, it successfully maintains reliable localization in building-less scenarios, completely overcoming the catastrophic failures of prior building-centric paradigms.

Computer Vision.title: Every Camera Effect, Every Time, All at Once: 4D Gaussian Ray Tracing for Physics-based Camera Effect Data Generation
Computer Vision.summary: Current video diffusion models can generate recognizable camera-effect appearances but do not reliably follow specified physical parameters such as field of view, aperture, and readout time, partly because real dynamic videos with diverse and accurate camera-effect annotations are scarce. Physics-based simulation provides exact labels but suffers from a sim-to-real gap. Reconstructing real dynamic scenes offers an alternative, but Dynamic NeRF methods render too slowly, whereas rasterization-based Dynamic Gaussian Splatting cannot model the light transport required by these effects. We propose 4D Gaussian Ray Tracing (4D-GRT), a two-stage data-generation pipeline that reconstructs dynamic scenes as 4D Gaussians from multi-view pinhole videos and re-renders them with physically based camera models under specified parameters. On CamVFX-4D, our controlled benchmark of eight dynamic indoor scenes under four camera effects, 4D-GRT achieves up to 3.4 dB higher PSNR and 6 times faster rendering than MSTH. Finally, we demonstrate two downstream applications: fine-tuning a video generation model on our data to improve camera-effect control and extending our pipeline to monocular input. Project page: https://shigon255.github.io/4DGRT-project-page/.
Computer Vision.comment: Paper accepted to WACV 2027. Project page: https://shigon255.github.io/4DGRT-project-page/

Computer Vision.title: Vision-based Sensing of Urban Environment using Hardware-Software co-design at Scale
Computer Vision.summary: Urban environmental monitoring is crucial for climate-adaptive cities, yet current approaches rely heavily on human inspection, overhead remote sensing, or limited terrestrial RGB imagery, thereby lacking comprehensive multispectral perspectives at street level. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces UrbanScapes, an adaptable and flexible hardware-software co-design platform for large-scale, vision-based sensing of urban environments. Built on a modular architecture, UrbanScapes seamlessly integrates multispectral imaging channels, including Red, Green, Blue (RGB), Near-Infrared, and Thermal, to capture multispectral street-level imagery. The system is designed for both opportunistic deployment on bicycles, vehicles, or pedestrians and targeted deployments on municipal fleets, ensuring high spatio-temporal scalability without requiring hardware redesigns. Crucially, the platform utilizes on-device deep learning models to automatically remove personally identifiable information (PII) at the edge, addressing privacy concerns inherent in street-level data collection. By combining this multispectral street-level imagery with overhead multispectral remote sensing imagery, UrbanScapes enables scalable calculation of physics-based environmental indices, providing a foundational tool for advanced citywide analysis.
Computer Vision.comment: IEEE World Forum for Internet of Things 2026

Computer Vision.title: Density-Aware Calibration for Resource-Efficient Medical Vision-Language Models
Computer Vision.summary: Medical vision-language models (VLMs) show promise for clinical image understanding, but their computational and memory requirements hinder deployment on resource-constrained clinical hardware. Post-training quantization (PTQ) offers a practical compression strategy without retraining, yet its effectiveness depends strongly on the calibration data. We propose CoreCalib, a training-free and quantizer-agnostic framework for constructing compact calibration sets that preserve the target medical VQA distribution. CoreCalib stratifies data by clinical question class, identifies representative visual modes using frozen DINOv2 features with UMAP and HDBSCAN, and expands selected images into class-balanced question-answer pairs. On Kvasir-VQA-x1, we evaluate CoreCalib with MASQuant, GPTQ, and QIG using a fixed 128-pair budget. CoreCalib achieves the best METEOR with all three quantizers and the best ROUGE-L with MASQuant and GPTQ. With W4A8 MASQuant, it improves METEOR from 0.5672 with COCO calibration to 0.6234, recovering approximately 41% of the degradation relative to BF16. These results support CoreCalib as a data-centric component for resource-efficient medical VLM deployment. Project page: https://magnusdtd.github.io/CoreCalib/ .

Computer Vision.title: Content-Preserving Principal Feature Blending for Training-Free Style Personalization
Computer Vision.summary: Reference-based style personalization should reproduce the appearance of a style reference while preserving the subject specified by a content prompt. In visual autoregressive models, dominant reference features can also carry object and spatial information, causing content leakage. We propose Content-Preserving Principal Feature Blending (CoPFB), a training-free method that estimates a low-rank content basis from a clean generation branch and removes the content-aligned component of the style residual. CoPFB applies rank-one blending at the first two autoregressive scales, followed by weaker content-projected refinement at the next three scales. On 1,900 combinations of Parti content prompts and FineStyle reference images, CoPFB improves text alignment from 0.293 to 0.297 and the harmonic score from 0.391 to 0.393 over PFB+SAC, while style similarity decreases from 0.590 to 0.577. CoPFB requires no fine-tuning or learnable parameters. Project page: https://vdkhoi20.github.io/CoPFB/.

Computer Vision.title: ROD-Dataset: A Pedestrian-Perspective Benchmark of Urban Obstacle Classes for YOLO-Based Detection
Computer Vision.summary: Two groups of pedestrians face avoidable risk on the city sidewalk: people living with visual impairment, who reach an obstacle before anything warns them, and people walking with divided attention, who register a hazard late or not at all.
